pieces.text: is money in the form of metal coins or paper bills. Cash has many advantages. It is quick and easy to use for small purchases. There are no extra fees or interest charges for using cash. Since cash is money that you physically hold and pay with, it is difficult to spend more money than you have. You don't need to have a bank account to use cash, either. Also, most businesses accept cash for in-person payments, even if they do not accept other forms of payment.

textContent.text: Cash also has several disadvantages. There is no easy way to prove ownership of cash. So, it is difficult to recover cash if it is lost, stolen, or destroyed. Cash also does not provide a record of your purchase if you lose your receipt. Additionally, online purchases cannot be made with cash. And many companies will not accept cash sent by mail.

pieces.text: A

is a piece of paper that lets you pay for something using the money in your bank account. With a check, you write down how much money you want to pay and who you are paying the money to. The other person takes the check to the bank to get the money.

textContent.text: Checks have many advantages. They give you access to all of the money in your bank account, without having to carry the cash with you. Checks can be canceled if they are lost or stolen, so they are safer to carry and send in the mail than cash. As long as you have enough money in your bank account, there are no extra fees for using checks. Checks also give you a record of your purchases to help keep track of your spending.

Checks also have several disadvantages. Writing a check takes longer than paying with cash. To have a checkbook, you need to open a checking account at a bank. If you write a check for more money than you have in your account, you will likely be charged fees by your bank and by the business that received your check. Some businesses will not accept checks, especially for online purchases. And criminals can steal checks and cash them, if you don't cancel missing checks right away.

is a piece of paper that lets you pay for something using the money in your bank account. With a check, you write down how much money you want to pay and who you are paying the money to. The other person takes the check to the bank to get the money.

textContent.text: Checks have many advantages. They give you access to all of the money in your bank account, without having to carry the cash with you. Checks can be canceled if they are lost or stolen, so they are safer to carry and send in the mail than cash. As long as you have enough money in your bank account, there are no extra fees for using checks. Checks also give you a record of your purchases to help keep track of your spending.

Checks also have several disadvantages. Writing a check takes longer than paying with cash. To have a checkbook, you need to open a checking account at a bank. If you write a check for more money than you have in your account, you will likely be charged fees by your bank and by the business that received your check. Some businesses will not accept checks, especially for online purchases. And criminals can steal checks and cash them, if you don't cancel missing checks right away.

As long as you have enough money in your bank account, there are no extra fees for using checks. Checks also give you a record of your purchases to help keep track of your spending.

Checks also have several disadvantages. Writing a check takes longer than paying with cash. To have a checkbook, you need to open a checking account at a bank. If you write a check for more money than you have in your account, you will likely be charged fees by your bank and by the business that received your check. Some businesses will not accept checks, especially for online purchases. And criminals can steal checks and cash them, if you don't cancel missing checks right away.

pieces.text: A

is a piece of paper that lets you pay for something using the money in your bank account. With a check, you write down how much money you want to pay and who you are paying the money to. The other person takes the check to the bank to get the money.

textContent.text: Checks have many advantages. They give you access to all of the money in your bank account, without having to carry the cash with you. Checks can be canceled if they are lost or stolen, so they are safer to carry and send in the mail than cash. As long as you have enough money in your bank account, there are no extra fees for using checks. Checks also give you a record of your purchases to help keep track of your spending.

Checks also have several disadvantages. Writing a check takes longer than paying with cash. To have a checkbook, you need to open a checking account at a bank. If you write a check for more money than you have in your account, you will likely be charged fees by your bank and by the business that received your check. Some businesses will not accept checks, especially for online purchases. And criminals can steal checks and cash them, if you don't cancel missing checks right away.

subheader.text: How can historians learn about daily life in the colonies?

subpoints.text: Historians can study the daily lives of colonial people by examining diaries, letters, and other records. For example, some 17th-century people kept diaries where they wrote about their daily activities.

Many English people settled in the New England Colonies for religious reasons. These settlers were motivated in part by divisions over religion in England in the 1600s. The English government supported a Christian church called the
. But some English people, including many settlers to New England, disagreed with the teachings of the Church of England.
Below are some leaders who lived in the New England Colonies. Which of these leaders settled in the New England Colonies for
reasons? Select all that apply.

labelDecorator.text: John Winthrop helped organize the Massachusetts Bay Colony based on what he saw as the rules of God.
Roger Williams was a minister who helped found Rhode Island. He wanted to live in a place where people could practice their religion freely.
Thomas Hooker was a minister who helped found Connecticut as a place where members of his church could live in peace.
Anne Hutchinson moved to the Massachusetts Bay Colony because she believed the Church of England was wrong.

The Paugusset group lived in western Connecticut, while the Mohegan, Pequot, and Niantic groups lived in eastern Connecticut. The Pequot lived near the Connecticut River. header.text: Colonists who settled in New England often had to adapt to the economic, or trading, practices of different Native American peoples. For example, in the adapted passage below, a New England colonist describes the economic practices of local Native American groups in the 1630s. Read the passage. Then answer the question below.

textContent.text: [The Natives] have a kind of beads instead of money, to buy such things as they want, which they call Wampum. It is of two sorts, the one is white, the other is of a violet color. These are made of the shells of fish. With these beads they buy and sell, not only amongst themselves, but even with us.

pieces.text: We sell them any of our
for this Wampum, because we know we can buy beaver furs with it: and these beads are currency in all the parts of New England, from one end of the coast to the other.

header.text: The adapted passage below was written by a New England colonist who fought in the Pequot War. In this passage, the colonist describes how an army of New England colonists and Native American allies attacked the most important Pequot town.

textContent.text: Many Pequot were burnt when we set fire to the town, men, women, and children, others forced out which our soldiers killed; down fell men, women, and children. Those that escaped us, fell into the hands of [the Native Americans fighting on the side of the colonists], that were behind us. There were about four hundred Pequot in this town, and not above five of them escaped out of our hands.
<citation>Captain John Underhill, Newes from America, 1638.</citation>

explanationText.text: England sometimes tried to eliminate other countries' control of trade by going to war with them.

content.text: passing laws to keep traders from the Netherlands out of English colonial ports

explanationText.text: Keeping traders from other countries away from North American ports was one way that the English controlled trade. Laws like these were meant to let English traders make money. explanationText.text: Laws such as these had to do with punishing criminals back in England. They would not have helped control trade in North America.

But over time, colonists began to grow enough food and other crops that they could sell some of what they grew. As a result, the economy of the Middle Colonies was largely based around growing
, or crops meant to be sold in places that could not grow them.

The New England colonies are shown as least fertile. The middle colonies are shown as most fertile, with some of the region being somewhat fertile. The Southern Colonies are shown as most fertile in all but a small area along the southern coast, which is shown as somewhat fertile. The other map shows the length of the growing season. The New England colonies have a growing season length of 3 to 5 or 5 to 7 months. The middle colonies are almost entirely shown as 5 to 7 months. The Southern colonies are labeled 7 to 9 months, except along the southern coast, where they are labeled 9 to 12 months.

The Middle Colonies had a

growing season than the Southern Colonies. The second map shows that the growing season in most of the Middle Colonies was 5 to 7 months. Most of the Southern Colonies had a growing season of 7 to 9 months.

The climate and growing conditions of the Middle Colonies allowed certain kinds of crops to grow well in the region. Early settlers to the Middle Colonies grew just enough food to survive. But over time, colonists began to grow enough food and other crops that they could sell some of what they grew. As a result, the economy of the Middle Colonies was largely based around growing
, or crops meant to be sold in places that could not grow them.

that apply.

choices.text: You sell some of your wheat in New England where a plant disease has made it hard to grow wheat.
You use the wheat to make flour to make bread that you and your family eat.
You sell the flour made from some of your wheat to slaveowners in the West Indies.
You give some of your wheat to a neighbor who uses the wheat to make bread to eat.

content.text: Many indentured servants in the colonies died of disease before their contracts ended.

elements.text: Disease killed many newcomers to the Southern Colonies. Indentured servants knew that they could die before they finished their contract.

content.text: Many landowners used punishments such as whipping to control their indentured servants.

elements.text: Many landowners treated their indentured servants badly. These punishments could lead to permanent injury or death.

pieces.text: These things were
, or possible benefits, for indentured servants:

content.text: Some indentured servants wanted to come to the colonies but could not pay for their journey. Landowners paid it for them.

elements.text: Traveling from Europe to North America was expensive. Poor Europeans could not afford the trip on their own.

content.text: Indentured servants often received land after their contracts ended.

elements.text: After a number of years, an indentured servant would usually be given some land in North America to farm. Land was expensive in Europe. For many poor Europeans, indentured servitude was the best chance of owning a farm.

, or possible dangers, for indentured servants:

content.text: Many indentured servants in the colonies died of disease.

elements.text: Disease killed many newcomers to the Southern Colonies. Indentured servants knew that they could die before they finished their contract.

content.text: Many landowners used physical punishments to control their indentured servants.

elements.text: Many landowners treated their indentured servants badly. These punishments could lead to permanent injury or death.

pieces.text: These things were
, or possible benefits, for indentured servants:

content.text: Landowners paid for the expensive journey to the colonies.

elements.text: Traveling from Europe to North America was expensive. Poor Europeans could not afford the trip on their own.

content.text: Indentured servants often received land after their contracts ended.

elements.text: After a number of years, an indentured servant would usually be given some land in North America to farm. Land was expensive in Europe. For many poor Europeans, indentured servitude was the best chance of owning a farm.

, or possible dangers, for indentured servants:

content.text: Many indentured servants in the colonies died of disease before their contracts ended.

elements.text: Disease killed many newcomers to the Southern Colonies. Indentured servants knew that they could die before they finished their contract.

content.text: Many landowners used punishments such as whipping to control their indentured servants.

elements.text: Many landowners treated their indentured servants badly. These punishments could lead to permanent injury or death.

pieces.text: These things were
, or possible benefits, for indentured servants:

content.text: Indentured servants often received land after their contracts ended.

elements.text: After a number of years, an indentured servant would usually be given some land in North America to farm. Land was expensive in Europe. For many poor Europeans, indentured servitude was the best chance of owning a farm.

content.text: Some indentured servants wanted to come to the colonies but could not pay for their journey. Landowners paid it for them.

elements.text: Traveling from Europe to North America was expensive. Poor Europeans could not afford the trip on their own.
